source_text: Circumcision is also associated with lower risks of penile cancer (odds ratio 0.33 in meta-analysis of case-control studies) and human papillomavirus (HPV)-related outcomes, though penile cancer remains exceedingly rare (1 in 100,000 annually in developed nations), necessitating over 900 circumcisions to prevent one case when performed neonatally.
